one_liner: Pure-Nim linear-time regex engine (PCRE-like syntax, no backtracking) beating PCRE2 on find-all throughput.
what_it_does: Provides regex parsing, compile-time or runtime compilation, and matching (match/find/findAll plus a match macro) for Nim programs, with PCRE-like syntax including named groups and lookaround. It is not a drop-in PCRE2 replacement: the API is re2"pattern" plus Regex2/RegexMatch2 objects, callable only from Nim (or via FFI wrapping from C). Regexes can be validated and compiled at compile time via Nim's macro system, catching syntax errors before runtime.
how_it_is_fast: Matching runs as a Thompson-style NFA simulation over parallel states (Pike's-VM approach, files nfamatch.nim/nfamatch2.nim use a `Pstates`/`Capts3` structure) rather than backtracking, giving match time linear in text and regex length. A literal-substring prefilter (litopt.nim, added in v0.22.0) skips ahead using known literal prefixes/substrings of the pattern, which is why the email-pattern benchmark result (1.32 ms vs PCRE2's 126.10 ms) dominates the aggregate speedup. Captures use a block-based capture array (space O(regex_len * groups_count)) instead of per-thread heap allocation.
when_to_use: Nim codebases that need to run regexes over untrusted input and want a hard linear-time guarantee instead of PCRE2's backtracking risk
Patterns with distinctive literal prefixes/substrings (email-, URL-, tag-style patterns) where the litopt prefilter gives large wins
Compile-time regex validation/compilation is wanted (re2"..." as a const catches syntax errors at compile time and avoids runtime compile cost)
Need PCRE-like syntax (character classes, named groups, lookaround) in Nim without adding a C PCRE2 dependency or FFI binding
Running inside Nim's compile-time VM, where linking a C library like PCRE2 isn't an option
when_not_to_use: Need to call the engine from C/C++/other languages without writing an FFI wrapper — PCRE2 is natively embeddable there, nim-regex is not
Pattern relies on backreferences or other non-regular PCRE features — explicitly unsupported to preserve the linear-time guarantee

Character-class-heavy patterns without literal anchors (e.g. pure IPv4-style patterns): in the optimized-PCRE2 run, PCRE2 beat nim-regex on the IPv4 pattern (4.73 ms vs 7.27 ms), and optimized Rust regex beat it overall
Need Unicode level 2/3 support (locale-aware casing, full normalization) — only Unicode level-1 is implemented

Feeding invalid/untrusted UTF-8 bytes in a release/danger build: UTF-8 validation is only performed in debug builds, so malformed input is undefined behavior (can hit an AssertionDefect) unless you pre-validate

integration.dependencies: none (pure Nim, stdlib only: std/unicode, std/tables, std/sets, std/algorithm, std/math, std/bitops)
integration.platforms: any platform Nim compiles to (pure Nim source, no SIMD/architecture-specific code observed)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same problem domain and PCRE-like syntax as PCRE2, but a distinct Nim-only API (re2/Regex2), not an ABI-compatible or FFI drop-in; the v0.21.0 release also broke nim-regex's own older API (re""/Regex -> re2""/Regex2)

gotchas: v0.21.0 deprecated the old re""/Regex/RegexMatch API in favor of re2""/Regex2/RegexMatch2 — check which API a given nimble version exposes
Only the last repetition of a repeated capture group is retained (same limitation as most regex engines), not all repetitions
Lookarounds that themselves contain repetition (*, +, {n,}) can run in polynomial time, breaking the library's headline linear-time guarantee

UTF-8 input validation is skipped in release/danger builds for performance; malformed UTF-8 is undefined behavior there, so untrusted text must be pre-validated (e.g. with validateUtf8 or nim-unicodeplus)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The other catalogued regex-engine entries (rejit, SafeRE, BLARE, RE#, coregex, nanoregex, re2jit) target C++/Rejit, Java, C++, .NET, Go/Rust-bench, or Python ecosystems; nim-regex is the only Nim-native option, so pick it when you're already in Nim and want PCRE2-beating throughput plus a no-backtracking safety guarantee without FFI, not when raw cross-language speedup magnitude is what matters.
verified_claims_summary: In mariomka/regex-benchmark's third-party cross-language shootout (find-all of email/URI/IPv4 patterns over a concatenated learnxinyminutes-docs corpus, on a 2019 MacBook Pro 16" i9, run in Docker), nim-regex (Nim 1.4.4, -d:release --opt:speed) totaled 36.09 ms versus C PCRE2 10.36-2's 251.37 ms (gcc -O3) and libstdc++ std::regex's 1023.49 ms (g++ -O3) in the default-settings table; with PCRE2 and Rust's regex crate both given their optimized/JIT builds, the PCRE2 gap narrows to ~2.6x (34.15 ms vs 87.87 ms) and optimized Rust regex (27.94 ms) comes out ahead of nim-regex.
status_note: Actively maintained — latest release v0.26.2 with recent "performance improvements" commits and last commit 2026-08-25; MIT-licensed pure-Nim source, small enough to vendor directly into a project.
